newsitem.title: UK: Tie Rack says profits below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Tie Rack says profits below expectations.

text.p: British retailer Tie Rack Plc said on Tuesday that current profits were slightly below expectations as a result of the strength of the pound.
The tie retailer told shareholders at its annual meeting that a further strengthening of the pound has continued to pressure overseas earnings.
Chief executive Nigel McGinley said that after a mixed sales performance in the spring, current sales trends had improved.
Tie Rack made pre-tax profits of 8.79 percent in the year to February 2, 1997, up 11 percent on the previous year.
The group, which has 422 shops with 60 percent of these overseas, plans to open another 25 more shops, predominantly outside the UK, in the remainder of the year.
